The levels of these nerves are represented by powerset plasmas $P_n$, which arise as algebraic realizations of representable $\Gamma$-sets, analogous to standard simplices in geometric realization.

papers.title: Instanton slices and their superpolynomials
papers.abstract:
The key theorem is a connection between motivic superpolynomials of plane curve singularities in any ranks with superpolynomials of the corresponding instanton slices, Nekrasov-type instanton sums with conductors. In this case, instanton slices are related to Compactified Jacobians, but they form a much wider class and, generally, have no connection to plane curve singularities. Thus, we extend significantly theory of affine Springer fibers in type A. For instance, we obtain a motivic interpretation (counting $\mathbb{F}_q$-points of some stacks) of superpolynomials for hyperbolic knots K12n242, K12n725, among many others. New formulas for Nekrasov's instanton sums as limits of superpolynomials of families of plane curve singularities are another application, with an impressive connection to nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials.
  The main conjecture states that instanton superpolynomials for arbitrary Young diagrams coincide with the corresponding (new) DAHA superpolynomials if and only if the latter are positive or (equivalently) the former are superdual. Only very few such diagrams come from plane curve singularities. Our DAHA superpolynomials are parallel to the EHA ones, but we used the nonsymmetric approach. The connection with Khovanov-Rozansky polynomials of the corresponding Coxeter knots is expected. Among applications: the Volume Conjecture reformulated in terms of instanton slices, topological invariance of unibranch motivic superpolynomials for semigroups with up to 4 generators, a mixed-characteristic conjecture, upgraded Weak Riemann Hypothesis, and superpolynomials for Gorenstein curve singularities and multibranch ones.

papers.title: Invariants of big classes from asymptotic total Betti numbers
papers.abstract: We introduce and study a new numerical invariant of big line bundles on normal complex projective varieties, defined in terms of the total Betti number of hypersurfaces associated with high tensor powers of the line bundle. We prove that this invariant is birational and provides an upper bound for the volume of the line bundle. When the big line bundle admits a rational Zariski decomposition, we show that the invariant coincides with the volume. In particular, this holds when the line bundle is ample or is defined on a projective surface. We also investigate the analogous problem in the real algebraic setting, proving the existence of real algebraic hypersurfaces associated with high tensor powers of a big line bundle whose real vanishing loci have arbitrarily large total Betti numbers.

papers.title: Isotropy of symplectic involutions and motivic equivalence for groups of type $\sf{C}$
papers.abstract: We extend to arbitrary characteristic a theorem due to Karpenko and Tignol on the isotropy of symplectic involutions after generic index reduction; as a consequence, we also prove the existence of critical varieties for semi-simple algebraic groups of type $\sf C$ over arbitrary base fields. The latter result relies on a characteristic-free argument, which involves the computation of the mod $2$ Tate trace of the variety of isotropic ideals of reduced dimension $2$ for a symplectic involution.

papers.title: Iterative construction of the R-matrices in arbitrary dimensions
papers.abstract:
We investigate a special ansats that allows for an iterative solution of the constant Yang-Baxter equation. Testing this ansatz, we construct four sequences of the constant R-matrices. In each sequence the R-matrices act on the tensor squares of vector spaces of linearly growing dimensions. Each R-matrix also depends on a single complex parameter.
  By analyzing the spectra of the R-matrices, we conclude that the first and the third series are associated with the symmetric tensor representations of the quantum groups U_q(sl(2)) and U_q(sl(2|1)), respectively. The other two series appear to be related to representations of quantum groups in the case where q is a root of unity. The elements of the second series are associated with nilpotent representations of U_q(sl(2)).
  We also check the correspondence between these R-matrices and link invariants. Applying the Reshetikhin-Turaev procedure to the first, second, and fourth sequences yields, respectively, colored Jones polynomials, ADO invariants, and Alexander polynomials. To our surprise, a similar calculation for the third series yields a trivial result, identically equal to 1.

papers.title: Jacobian rings and the infinitesimal Torelli Theorem
papers.abstract: In this article we deal with jacobian rings and identify a mixed Hodge component of a nondegenerate hypersurface in the torus with a lattice geometric quotient vector space. We introduce a period map, study its differential and compute the kernel of the differential much explicitly via certain Laurent polynomials. As a main application we deal with the infinitesimal Torelli theorem (ITT). We study the kernel of the cohomological map for explicit deformations and complete our study by dealing with the remaining part $\coker(\kappa_{\mathbb{P},f})$ (cokernel of the Kodaira-Spencer map) in dimensions $n \geq 4$.

papers.title: James reduced product schemes and double quasisymmetric functions
papers.abstract:
Symmetric function theory is a key ingredient in the Schubert calculus of Grassmannians. Quasisymmetric functions are analogues that are similarly central to algebraic combinatorics, but for which the associated geometry is poorly developed. Baker and Richter (2008) showed that $\operatorname{QSym}$ manifests topologically as the cohomology ring of the loop suspension of infinite projective space or equivalently of its combinatorial homotopy model, the James reduced product $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$. In recent work, we used this viewpoint to develop topologically-motivated bases of $\operatorname{QSym}$ and initiate a Schubert calculus for $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$ in both cohomology and $K$-theory.
  Here, we study the torus-equivariant cohomology of $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$. We identify a cellular basis and introduce double monomial quasisymmetric functions as combinatorial representatives, analogous to the factorial Schur functions and double Schubert polynomials of classical Schubert calculus. We also provide a combinatorial Littlewood--Richardson-type rule for the structure coefficients of this basis.
  Furthermore, we introduce an algebro-geometric analogue of the James reduced product construction. In particular, we prove that the James reduced product of a complex (quasi-)projective variety also carries the structure of a (quasi-)projective variety.

papers.title: K\"ahler-Ricci Flow is Symplectic Deflation plus an Exact Symplectic Deformation
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that K\"ahler-Ricci flow on a Fano surface decomposes as a symplectic deflation along a plurianticanonical divisor plus an exact symplectic deformation in the divisor complement. We apply this decomposition to the study of certain projective bundles. We establish the optimal decay rate in the setting of Song, Sz\'ekelyhidi, and Weinkove for a family of toric metrics which match the cohomological profile of K\"ahler-Ricci flow. In doing so, we identify a $C^2$-obstruction to proving the optimal decay rate in the setting of ruled toric surfaces. We present these ideas as a new symplectic-topological approach to the study of K\"ahler-Ricci flow.

papers.title: Kawamata-Viehweg and Lipman's vanishings for sequences of blow-ups at regular closed points
papers.abstract: The birational Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing theorem (KVV for short) is known to hold in considerable generality in equal characteristic zero, but fails in general in positive characteristic. We study a vanishing conjecture of Lipman for sequences of blow-ups at closed points of the spectrum of a regular local ring. We prove the conjecture when the ring has dimension at most three. We also establish a relative Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing theorem for exceptional nef Q-divisors when all blow-up centers are rational over the residue field and the positive residue characteristic is at least the dimension of the ring minus one. Both results allow mixed characteristic.

papers.title: Koszul Duality for Quadratic Monomial Algebras
papers.abstract: Let \(\Lambda\) be a quadratic monomial algebra and let \(\Lambda^{!}\) denote its Koszul dual. We study finitely presented and finitely copresented graded modules over \(\Lambda\) and \(\Lambda^{!}\), and use this structure to obtain explicit forms of derived and singular Koszul duality. We prove that quadratic monomial algebras are both graded coherent and graded cocoherent. Applying this to the Koszul dual \(\Lambda^{!}\), which is again quadratic monomial, we show that finitely presented and finitely copresented graded \(\Lambda^{!}\)-modules coincide with perfect and coperfect modules, respectively. It follows that the corresponding tails and cotails categories are hereditary abelian categories, and their objects are described in terms of linear and colinear modules. We also prove that quadratic monomial algebras are absolutely Koszul and have global linearity defect at most two. Consequently, finite-dimensional graded \(\Lambda\)-modules have rational Poincar\'e series, while finitely presented and finitely copresented graded \(\Lambda^{!}\)-modules have rational Hilbert series. As applications, we refine graded and ungraded derived Koszul dualities, singular Koszul dualities, and Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand correspondences for quadratic monomial algebras. We further describe the induced nonstandard \(t\)-structures on bounded derived and singularity categories and derive bounds for the finitistic dimension of \(\Lambda\) in terms of finite paths in the Koszul dual algebra.

papers.title: LandscapeSHAP: Which Persistent Homology Class Gets the Credit?
papers.abstract: Shapley values, a solution concept from cooperative game theory, have recently become a standard tool for feature credit allocation in machine learning. They provide an axiomatically justified method to fairly distribute a model's prediction among the data features. Shapley values have not yet been applied to explain machine learning models trained on features from topological data analysis. We develop what we believe is the first such approach, focusing on the persistence landscape featurization of persistence diagrams. Because each landscape coordinate is a rank statistic, crediting a model's prediction back to individual persistent homology classes (persistence diagram points) is nontrivial. We introduce LandscapeSHAP, a method for fair credit allocation to persistence diagram points based on a model's prediction. For linear models on persistence landscapes, LandscapeSHAP has a closed form expression that gives the exact Shapley value of every persistence diagram point. In particular, there is no coalition sampling required. We further prove that the four Shapley "fairness" axioms uniquely characterize this credit allocation for any model, not only linear ones. For a general nonlinear model, this unique value can only be calculated exactly from its defining coalition averaging formula, which requires considering all $2^N$ many coalitions, where $N$ is the number of points in the persistence diagram. This is computationally intractable for persistence diagrams of realistic size. We complement the exact linear model result with an efficient Monte Carlo sampling of persistence diagram coalitions. We give convergence rates in terms of number of samples needed to approximate to a desired degree of accuracy. We also prove stability results for the LandscapeSHAP credit allocation, for any model.

papers.title: Langlands Duality and Invariant Differential Operators: the Case SL(2n+1)
papers.abstract: Recently we started building a bridge between two cases of Langlands duality. The latter is one of the most influential topics in mathematical research. It has many different appearances and influential subtopics. Yet there is a topic that until now seems unrelated to the Langlands program. That is the topic of invariant differential operators. That is strange since both items are deeply rooted in Harish-Chandra's representation theory of semisimple Lie groups. We started with the case of the group ~$SL(2n)$. In the present paper we deal with the group $SL(2n+1)$. The two mentioned groups are similar, but their representation theories is rather different.

papers.title: Lefschetz Properties of complete intersesctions and maximal variation of hyperplane sections
papers.abstract: For an artinian complete intersection of forms of degree $d$, we prove that the multiplication by a general linear form is injective up to degree $\frac{3d-1}2$, independently of the number of variables. This is accomplished using algebraic and geometric properties of the union of two complete intersection curves and their general hyperplane sections. As a consequence, we solve, for any $d\ge 4$, the problem about the maximal variation of the hyperplane sections of a smooth hypersurface of degree $d$ posed by A. Beauville.

papers.title: Local Converse Theorems for $k$-Middle Supercuspidal Representations of $p$-adic $\text{GL}(kn)$
papers.abstract: Let $\text{F}$ be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero with residual characteristic $p$. In this paper, we study local converse theorems for $k$-middle supercuspidal representations of $\text{GL}(kn, \text{F})$ via explicit computations of twisted gamma factors on the Galois side, under the assumptions $p \nmid kn$ and $q_{\text{F}}>(k-1)^2$. Our results provide further evidence for a conjecture of the third-named author and Stevens on depth bounds for the twisting representations in the local converse theorem. For odd $k \ge 3$, we obtain infinitely many families of supercuspidal representations for which the bound $\left\lfloor \frac{kn}{2} \right\rfloor$ in the local converse theorem is not sharp.

papers.title: Lusztig's asymptotic algebra and a cell factorisation for the second lowest two-sided cell in type $\tilde{B}_n$
papers.abstract: We determine Lusztig's asymptotic algebra for the second lowest two-sided cell~$\Delta_1$ in the equal parameter extended affine Weyl group $\tilde{\mathsf{B}}_n$ for all $n\geq 2$, realising it as a full matrix algebra over the representation ring of $\mathsf{Sp}_{2n-2}(\CC)\times C_2$ with $C_2$ the group of order~$2$. Our result is an explicit isomorphism of based rings, determining the image of each basis element $\mathsf{t}_w$ of the asymptotic algebra. As a consequence we verify that Lusztig's original conjecture from 1989 on the structure of the asymptotic algebra holds for this cell. A key ingredient in our proof is a refinement of Shi's description of~$\Delta_1$, giving an explicit parametrisation of the elements of this cell (a \textit{cell factorisation}). This cell factorisation simultaneously describes all intersections of left and right cells, with uniqueness and length-additivity of expressions. Applications include a classification of the involutions in $\Delta_1$, and a calculation of the length generating functions for $\Delta_1$ and the right cells in~$\Delta_1$.

papers.title: M\"obius functions for pseudo-Levi subgroups in finite general linear and symplectic groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we compute the M\"obius function on the poset of pseudo-Levi subgroups containing a fixed maximal torus of two families of finite groups, $GL_n(q)$ and $Sp_{2n}(q)$, for some natural number $n$ and a prime power $q$, where $q>2n+1$. For the general linear group, we consider arbitrary tori, but for symplectic groups, we restrict to tori corresponding to the bipartitions of $n$ into odd integers. Also, we assume $q$ is even for the case of symplectic groups. The M\"obius function for the set of pseudo-Levi subgroups of a finite group $G$ is important for an explicit evaluation of the formula expressing the decomposition of tensor products of characters, as proved in Theorem 2 of the paper ''Multiplicity of characters of finite reductive groups and Drinfeld doubles'' [arXiv:2512.01432].

papers.title: Mellin transformed exponential volumes and probabilistic moduli spaces
papers.abstract:
A decorated surface is a surface with boundary and a finite set of marked boundary points called cusps. We continue to study the exponential volumes E(S,K,L) of moduli spaces of ideal hyperbolic structures on a decorated surface S, with the given values of lengths of boundary geodesic circles L and boundary geodesic intervals K, introduced in our previous work:
  1. We prove that the Mellin--Laplace transform of E(S,K,L) admits Barnes integral presentations, and satisfies recursions, generalising Mirzakhani's recursions.
  2. We specify a subset I of the blue boundary intervals, and assign to them any collection of weights. We show that the Mellin transform of the function E(S,K,L) along the variables K at the blue intervals, evaluated at the weights values, calculates weighted exponential volumes of various moduli spaces. If all boundary intervals are blue and all weights are 1/2, we recover Chekhov's volumes of moduli spaces of hyperbolic surfaces with crowns, discretizing the Schwarzian action. We derive recursions for the weighted exponential volumes.
  3. We introduce probabilistic Teichmuller spaces related to decorated surfaces S. They are infinite dimensional and carry canonical Wiener type measures. The definition of the measures builds on the works of Bauerschmidt - Losev - Wildemann and Losev. Their quotients by the action of the modular group of S are probabilistic moduli spaces. We show that their volumes are finite. We prove recursion formulas for these measures, and hence for the volumes.
  The emerging theory generalizes the Schwarzian field theory of Stanford - Witten from the disc to any decorated surfaces, i.e. to open string format. In particular, we get recursions for the Feynman integrals in Schwarzian field theory on decorated surfaces.

papers.title: Meromorphic modular differential equations for the elliptic genus of Calabi--Yau varieties
papers.abstract: We study differential equations -- not necessarily monic -- for Jacobi modular forms. As an application, we derive a second-order differential equation for the elliptic genus of a $K3$ surface involving the logarithmic derivative of the modular invariant $j(\tau)$, and we explicitly find a third-order equation with a leading coefficient of weight 12 for the elliptic genus of any four-dimensional Calabi--Yau variety. Furthermore, we propose a simple recursive algorithm for investigating second-order differential equations with leading coefficient $E_4(\tau)$ or $E_6(\tau)$.

papers.title: Millicharged particles and the degree-3 Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem
papers.abstract:
We use geometry to solve a problem in arithmetic relevant for physics. Namely, for any $m$ we find all integer solutions to the equations $\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^k = \sum_{i=1}^m y_i^k$, where $k \in \{1,2,3\}$; this seems to be new for $m \geq 5$.
  In physics, these are the anomaly cancellation conditions for models with $m$ fermions which can be naturally light and carry small electric charges (a.k.a. millicharged or minicharged particles). The small charges arise by kinetic mixing of the Standard Model $U(1)$ gauge symmetry with an unbroken non-chiral (a.k.a. vector-like) $U(1)$ and the masses are suppressed by a spontaneously-broken chiral $U(1)$.

papers.title: Moments and Large Geometric Monodromy for Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families
papers.abstract: Let $q=p^a$ with $p$ prime, $\lambda\in\mathbb F_p^\times$, and $\psi_q=\psi\circ\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}$ for a nontrivial additive character $\psi$ of $\mathbb F_p$. For $n\ge2$ we study $\Sigma_n(h)=\sum_{u\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n,\sum_i h_i u_i=-\lambda}\psi_q(\sum_i u_i^{-1})$. On $\mathbb G_m^n$ we construct a lisse sheaf $\mathcal W_n$, pure of weight $n+1$ and rank $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, whose Frobenius traces equal $(-1)^{n-1}q\Sigma_n(h)$ minus an explicit polynomial in $q$, for $h\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$. For odd $p$, its geometric monodromy has identity component $\mathrm{SL}_{r(n)}$ and cyclic component group of order divisible by $p$. The full group is $\{g:\det(g)^p=1\}$ for $n=2$, and for $n\ge3$ using boundary unipotence from the companion preprint arXiv:2610.03081. For $p=2$, the sheaf is self-dual and its geometric monodromy is $\mathrm{SO}_{r(n)}$ for odd $n$ and $\mathrm{Sp}_{r(n)}$ for even $n$. After normalization to weight zero, the arithmetic and geometric groups coincide, using the same companion input for odd $p$ and $n\ge3$. As $q\to\infty$ with $p$ fixed, we obtain Sato-Tate laws for centered, normalized sums with error $O(q^{-1/2})$ for polynomial tests and formulas for all power moments. For $p=2$, limiting moments are Gaussian through order $r(n)-1$, with an excess of one above the orthogonal value at order $r(n)$ for odd $n$; if $n+1$ is a power of two, every Frobenius on $\mathcal W_n$ has eigenvalue $q^{(n+1)/2}$. The proof uses $\sum_h|\Sigma_n(h)|^4=c_pq^{3n-2}+O(q^{3n-2-\delta(n)})$ for $n\ge3$, where $c_p=2$ for odd $p$, $c_2=3$ and $\delta(n)=\min(1,(n-2)/2)$, plane sections of the Cayley cubic, exact Frobenius-Schur identities, Laumon's local Fourier transforms and Artin-Schreier theory. For $n=2$ we identify twisted classical Kloosterman sums and compute the fourth moment exactly.

papers.title: MONODROMY AND BIG QUANTUM COHOMOLOGY OF HYPERPLANE SECTIONS OF (CO)ADJOINT VARIETIES
papers.abstract: We study the monodromy representation of general hyperplane sections of (co)adjoint varieties. We apply this result to reduce the generic semisemplicity of the big quantum cohomology to its ambient part, and to prove that the big quantum cohomology of general hyperplane sections of IGr(2, 6) is generically semisimple and satisfies Dubrovin's conjecture.

papers.title: Morita equivalent blocks with an endotrivial source that are not globally isotypic
papers.abstract: Let $(K,\mathcal{O},k)$ be a large enough $2$-modular system. We construct two nilpotent block algebras of finite groups which are isomorphic as $\mathcal{O}$-algebras and are Morita equivalent via a bimodule with an endotrivial source of $\mathcal{O}$-rank $3$, but which are not globally isotypic. Hence they are not $2$-permutation equivalent and not splendidly Rickard equivalent. These results separate Morita equivalences with endopermutation source from $p$-permutation equivalences and splendid Rickard equivalences, and also separate almost global isotypies from global isotypies.

papers.title: Negative Values of Wahl's Second Chern Number for Normal Surface Singularities
papers.abstract: We disprove Wahl's 1993 vanishing conjecture, open for more than thirty years, which asserts that $c_2^w(X)=0$ for every nonquotient normal surface singularity. Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve with a nontrivial involution having $r>0$ fixed points, and put $d=2g(C)-2$. If $d>r$, the union of the diagonal and the graph of the involution in $C\times C$ has negative definite intersection matrix and can be analytically contracted to a normal surface singularity $(X,o)$. A direct relative Chern-class computation and Wahl's residue formula give $c_2^w(X)=-r(d+r)/(d-r)$. An explicit curve of genus four gives $c_2^w(X)=-4$. Branched double covers of a fixed curve of genus two yield examples with $c_2^w(X_m)=-2m(m+1)$, so these values are unbounded below. We give the construction and intersection calculations in detail, as well as a line-bundle filtration realizing the negative value.

papers.title: Non-canonical Oscillator Representations of Orthogonal Lie Algebras and Pfaffian Varieties
papers.abstract: Associated varieties are fundamental geometric invariants in the study of infinite-dimensional representations of semisimple Lie algebras. Luo and Xu (2013) constructed a large family of infinite-dimensional irreducible representations of orthogonal Lie algebras by applying Fourier transforms to the natural oscillator representations. In this paper, we prove that the associated varieties of these irreducible representations are isomorphic to explicitly described coordinate linear sections of Pfaffian varieties. The modules are realized as spaces of polynomial solutions of transformed Laplace equations. We construct filtrations from weighted polynomial degrees and determine the annihilator ideals of the corresponding associated graded modules. The defining equations consist of linear coordinate equations, minors and quadratic Pfaffian relations. The even and odd orthogonal Lie algebras are treated separately. The associated varieties are viewed as reduced affine schemes over a field of characteristic zero. In each irreducible family with fixed Fourier parameters, the associated variety is independent of the grading parameter. When the two Fourier parameters coincide, the projectivizations in the even case are Grassmannians.

papers.title: Non-existence of Negative Weight Derivations of the Moduli Algebras of Isolated Weighted Homogeneous Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: Mather and Yau proved that the analytic isomorphism class of an isolated complex hypersurface singularity is determined by its dimension and its moduli algebra. Yau's conjecture asserts that the moduli algebra of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity over $\mathbb{C}$ has no nonzero derivation of negative degree. We prove this conjecture. The proof uses Varchenko\textquotesingle s theorem on the $\mu$-constant stratum of an isolated weighted homogeneous singularity, also stated by M. Saito.

papers.title: Non-existence of negative weight derivations on Jacobian algebras
papers.abstract: Let $S=\mathbb K[x_1,\cdots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring in $n$ variables with positive integer weights over a field $\mathbb K$ of characteristic zero. Let $f\in S$ be a weighted homogeneous polynomial such that the Jacobian algebra $$A=\left.S \middle/ \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1},\cdots,\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_n}\right)\right.$$ is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb K$-vector space. We prove that $A$ has no nonzero negative weight derivation, which confirms a conjecture of the third author. An immediate consequence of this conjecture is the micro-local characterization of quasi-homogeneous singularities.

papers.title: On a specialization of Toda eigenfunctions
papers.abstract: This paper studies rational functions $\mathfrak{J}_\alpha(q)$, which depend on a positive element $\alpha$ of the root lattice of a root system. These functions arise as Shapovalov pairings of Whittaker vectors in Verma modules of highest weight $-\rho$ for quantum groups and as Hilbert series of Zastava spaces, and are related to the Toda system. They are specializations of multivariate functions more commonly studied in the literature. We investigate the denominator of these rational functions and give an explicit combinatorial formula for the numerator in type A. We also propose a conjectural realization of the numerator as the Poincar\'e polynomial of a smooth variety in type A.

papers.title: On an example of Aspinwall, Morrison, and Szendr\H{o}i
papers.abstract: We study the cohomology of a 1-parameter family Y_t of Calabi-Yau 3-folds introduced by Aspinwall and Morrison, related to the mirror quintic family. Szendr\H{o}i proved that Y_t, Y_{xi t}, ..., Y_{xi^4 t}, where xi is a fifth root of unity, have the same rational Hodge structure but are not isomorphic, and conjectured that they are not birational or even derived equivalent. We confirm this by proving that their integral Hodge structures are different, and discuss how this fits with known Torelli-type theorems and counterexamples.

papers.title: On arrangements of plane real quartics with respect to three lines
papers.abstract: We complete the classification of mutual arrangements of a smooth real algebraic or real pseudoholomorphic quartic curve and three lines under condition that each oval of the quartic intersects the union of the lines. This classification was started in a recent preprint by Maletto. There is one arrangement which is realizable pseudoholomorphically but not algebraically. It can be constructed in different ways, in particular, by a combinatorial patchworking on an irregular triangulation. This is the first example of a combinatorial patchworking which produces a PL curve in $RP^2$ whose arrangement relative to the coordinate axes is algebraically unrealizable.

papers.title: On certain Lagrangian subvarieties in minimal resolutions of Kleinian singularities
papers.abstract: Kleinian singularities are quotients of $\mathbb{C}^2$ by finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$. They are in bijection with the simply-laced Dynkin diagrams via the McKay correspondence. Anti-Poisson involutions and their fixed point loci appear naturally in the classification of irreducible Harish-Chandra modules over Kleinian singularities. There are three goals of this paper. The first is to classify anti-Poisson involutions of Kleinian singularities up to conjugation by graded Poisson automorphisms. The second is to describe the scheme-theoretic fixed point loci of Kleinian singularities under anti-Poisson involutions. The third and main goal is to describe the scheme-theoretic preimages of the fixed point loci under minimal resolutions of Kleinian singularities. These preimages are singular Lagrangian subvarieties in the minimal resolutions whose irreducible components are $\mathbb{P}^1$'s and $\mathbb{A}^1$'s. Additionally, we discuss the connections between anti-Poisson involutions and Lie algebra involutions.

papers.title: On elements of degree $g$ in the separating semigroup of a real curve of genus $g$
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be a separating real algebraic curve of genus $g$ whose real locus consists of $r$ components and let $S=\mathrm{Sep}(C)$ be its separating semigroup. An element $\delta\in S$ is called extendable if $\delta+\mathbb N_0^r\subset S$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{n\in\mathbb Z\mid n\ge 0\}$. We prove that an element of $S$ is extendable if it is realizable by a separating mobile divisor of degree $g$ and projective rank 1.

papers.title: On infinite accumulation points of log canonical volumes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a new phenomenon in the geography of volumes: for every integer $d\geq 2$, the set of volumes of $d$-dimensional projective log canonical varieties has an infinite accumulation point.

papers.title: On maximal curves of $n$-correct sets
papers.abstract: Suppose $\mathcal{X}$ is an $n$-correct set of nodes in the plane, that is, it admits a unisolvent interpolation with bivariate polynomials of total degree less than or equal to $n.$ Then an algebraic curve $q$ of degree $k\le n$ can pass through at most $d(n,k):={{n+2}\choose {2}}-{{n+2-k}\choose {2}}$ nodes of $\mathcal{X}$. A curve $q$ of degree $k\le n$ is called maximal if it passes through exactly $d(n,k)$ nodes of $\mathcal{X}$. In particular, a maximal line is a line passing through $d(n,1)=n+1$ nodes of $\mathcal{X}$. Maximal curves are an important tool for the study of $n$-correct sets. We present new properties of maximal curves, as well as extensions of known properties.

papers.title: On solutions to tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations
papers.abstract: This paper develops convex analysis on tropical varieties and investigates the properties of the tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations. We start by introducing notions of plurisubharmonic functions and K\"ahler forms on arbitrary tropical varieties. We show that many classical results of pluripotential theory extend to this setting, including an analogue of Demailly's regularization theorem. Next, we study the solutions to the tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations. While we establish their uniqueness, we show that the existence is not guaranteed in general. More precisely, we prove that the tropical analogue of the Calabi-Yau theorem fails for any pair $(X, \theta)$ consisting of a compact tropical variety $X$ of dimension at least two satisfying a mild genericity assumption, and a tropical K\"ahler form $\theta$ on $X$. In particular, there exist measures compactly supported in the open part of $X$ that admit no solution. In contrast, for tropical varieties that are regular in codimension one, we show the existence of solutions. Finally, via strongly faithful tropicalizations whose existence is established in this paper, we relate the tropical solutions, when they exist, to the solutions of non-Archimedean Monge-Amp\`ere equations on Berkovich spaces.

papers.title: On the $v$-adic values of $G$-functions
papers.abstract:
We study $G$-functions centered at smooth fibers of one--parameter families of principally polarized abelian varieties. Building on work of Yves Andr\'e, we associate to such families a collection of $G$-functions whose local values admit period interpretations at archimedean places and at finite places of good reduction of the distinguished fiber, and whose radii of convergence control reduction-theoretic proximity at the latter places. We also discuss a conjectural extension to places of bad semistable reduction using Hyodo--Kato cohomology.
  Specializing to $\mathcal{A}_2$, we construct non-trivial algebraic relations among the values of these $G$-functions at $E^2$- and $E\times\mathrm{CM}$-points in both the archimedean and $p$-adic settings. At non-supersingular finite places of good reduction, we construct relations independent of the place. Finally, we obtain height bounds via Andr\'e-Bombieri's Hasse principle and discuss applications to large Galois orbit estimates and Zilber--Pink finiteness results for curves in $\mathcal{A}_2$.

papers.title: On The Acyclic MacPhersonian
papers.abstract:
The acyclic MacPhersonian $\AM_n^d$ is the poset of acyclic oriented matroids of rank $d+1$ on $n$ labelled elements, the combinatorial model of the space of configurations of $n$ points spanning $\R^d$ up to affine equivalence, which is the Grassmannian $G(d,n-1)$. We study it inside the larger poset $\Sep_n^d$ of \emph{spherical separoids}, those acyclic separoids whose Radon complex is a sphere of the dimension of the space of affine dependences.
  Our main unconditional results are as follows. Over every poset of spherical separoids that contains the realizable oriented matroids there is a tautological sphere fibration, and its Stiefel--Whitney classes show that the mod~$2$ cohomology ring of $G(d,n-1)$ is a ring retract of that of the poset, for all $n$ and $d$. For $d=n-2$ the poset of spherical separoids is homotopy equivalent to $G(n-2,n-1)$, and contains $\AM_n^{n-2}$ as a homotopy equivalent subposet. A fat model of $\AM_n^d$ made of piecewise geodesic antipodal spheres in the round sphere is weakly homotopy equivalent to its order complex. The chirotope of every such sphere is recovered from the degrees of its coordinate projections.
  We then analyse a strategy based on the mean curvature flow. Any argument that follows the combinatorial type of a sphere generically along the flow would connect every uniform oriented matroid to a realizable one by mutations. By a theorem of Gu and Knauer this is impossible in every rank $r\ge7$ on $n\ge r+17$ elements, so the flow must leave the oriented matroids. We show that the basin hypothesis of the flow, together with the property that $\|\AM_n^d\|$ is a homology manifold, implies $\|\AM_n^d\|\simeq G(d,n-1)$, without following types along the flow. We conclude with the open problems and conjectures that remain.

papers.title: On the classification of threefold flops
papers.abstract: We show that possibly singular threefold flopping contractions are completely classified by their associated derived contraction algebras, considered up to derived Morita equivalence; in contrast to the smooth case the extra derived structure is necessary in general. This extends previous work of the author on simple flops, and follows from a more general theorem about isolated hypersurface singularities. The key new input is to show that derived localisation at a Hochschild class is Morita invariant; this result raises some interesting questions related to the classification of recollements. We also show that derived contraction algebras admit a deformation-theoretic interpretation in families in a general setting that encompasses threefold flops, flips, and divisor-to-curve contractions.

papers.title: On the hyperplane conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the hyperplane conjecture, proposed by Hosono, Lian, and Yau in arXiv:alg-geom/9511001 and its generalization to orbifolds. Consequently, this establishes the expected equivalence between the \(A\) model (genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants with ambient insertions) of \(X\) and the \(B\) model (period integrals corresponding to vanishing cohomology) of \(X^{\vee}\) for Batyrev's mirror pair of Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces. As an application of our method, we also identify the residue of the Gauss--Manin connection and the cup product morphism on the \(A\)-side.

papers.title: On The Manin Constant
papers.abstract: We prove the Manin constant conjecture for every optimal elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ and Stevens' Conjectures I and II. Our method adapts Hongbo Yin's congruence argument for cubic roots of modular functions to lifts of modular parametrizations through isogenies, using the unbounded denominators theorem of Calegari, Dimitrov and Tang.

papers.title: On the moduli space of stable surfaces with $p_g=1$ realizing the minimal volume
papers.abstract:
Let $M_1$ be the moduli space of the KSBA stable surfaces $X$ of geometric genus $p_g(X)=1$ realizing the minimal possible volume $K_X^2=\frac1{143}$. We show that $M_{1}$ is a $10$-dimensional weighted projective space. By a result of Brieskorn, it is isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification $\overline{F}_\Lambda^{\mathrm{BB}}$ of the moduli space of $\Lambda$-polarized K3 surfaces, where $\Lambda=\mathrm{II}_{1,9}\simeq U\oplus E_8$ is a unimodular lattice of signature $(1,9)$.
  More generally, let $M_c$ be the moduli space $M_c$ of KSBA stable surface pairs $(X,B)$ with coefficients of $B$ belonging to a set $\mathcal{C}\subset (0,1]$ such that $\mathcal{C}\cup\{1\}$ attains a minimum, say $c$, and with $p_g(X)=1$, realizing the minimal possible volume $(K_X+B)^2=v(c)$. We show that the reduced part $M_{c,\mathrm{red}}$ is independent of~$c$ and that for $c\leq\frac{7}{13}$ or $c\geq \frac{6}{11}$, $M_c$ is isomorphic to $\overline{F}_\Lambda^\mathrm{BB}$. Up to normalization, we provide a geometric interpretation of this isomorphism using the Kulikov model.
  We also verify the Viehweg hyperbolicity of the base of a Whitney equisingular family of stable surface pairs in $M_c$.

papers.title: On the number of cokernel-closed additive subcategories for uniformly oriented $A_n$ quivers
papers.abstract: We study the integer sequence that enumerates cokernel-closed, idempotent split, full, additive subcategories of the category of finite dimensional complex representations of a uniformly oriented $A_n$ quiver. Using a combinatorial model, we describe a non-obvious connection of this sequence to Catalan numbers and derive an implicit recurrence. We also describe some basic properties of the lattice underlying the sequences, in particular, we give an explicit description of the meet irreducible elements of that lattice.

papers.title: Parabolic Simple $\mathscr{L}$-Invariants
papers.abstract: Let $L$ be a finite extension of $\mathbf{Q}_p$. Let $\rho_L$ be a potentially semi-stable non-crystalline $p$-adic Galois representation such that the associated $F$-semisimple Weil-Deligne representation is absolutely indecomposable. In this paper, we study Fontaine-Mazur parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants of $\rho_L$, which was previously only known in the trianguline case. Based on the previous work on Breuil's parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants, we attach to $\rho_L$ a locally $\mathbf{Q}_p$-analytic representation $\Pi(\rho_L)$ of $\mathrm{GL}_{n}(L)$, which carries the information of parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants of $\rho_L$. When $\rho_L$ comes from a patched automorphic representation of $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A}_{F^+})$ (for a define unitary group $\mathbf{G}$ over a totally real field $F^+$ which is compact at infinite places and $\mathrm{GL}_n$ at $p$-adic places), we prove under mild hypothesis that $\Pi(\rho_L)$ is a subrepresentation of the associated Hecke-isotypic subspace of the Banach spaces of (patched) $p$-adic automophic forms on $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A}_{F^+})$, this is equivalent to say that the Breuil's parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants are equal to Fontaine-Mazur parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants.

papers.title: Partial actions of inverse categories and their algebras
papers.abstract: In this work we introduce partial and global actions of inverse categories on posets in two variants, fibred actions and actions by symmetries. We study in detail actions of an inverse category $\mathcal{C}$ on specific subposets of the poset of finite subsets of $\mathcal{C}$, the Bernoulli actions. We show that to each fibred action of an inverse category on a poset there corresponds another inverse category, the semidirect product associated to the action. The Bernoulli actions give rise to the Szendrei expansions of $\mathcal{C}$, which define an endofunctor of the category of inverse categories. We extend the concept of ''enlargement'' from inverse semigroup theory to inverse categories, and we show that if $\mathcal{D}$ is an enlargement of $\mathcal{C}$ then their Cauchy completions are equivalent categories; in particular, some pairs corresponding to partial and global Bernoulli actions are enlargements. We conclude by studying convolution algebras of finite inverse categories and showing that if $\mathcal{D}$ is an enlargement of $\mathcal{C}$ then their convolution algebras are Morita equivalent. Furthermore, using Kan extensions we also analyze the infinite case.

papers.title: Pellarin Values from Cauchy Coordinates on Arbitrary Curves
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be the ring of functions regular outside a closed point of degree $\mathrm{N}$ on a smooth projective curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We express the normalized weight-one ideal Pellarin value of a rank-one Drinfeld $A$-module as an ordinary Hilbert-class trace of rational Cauchy differentials. A pairing on projective period lattices identifies the differential associated with each ideal class and computes its coefficients by finite torsion traces. For a nonfree lattice, the formula uses an isogeny with arbitrary nonzero derivative to a module with free period lattice. Each ideal-class subseries extends regularly to the characteristic point with value one, so the full series takes the value $|\operatorname{Cl}(A)|$. For every rank-one module, the quotient of the Anderson generating differential by the Drinfeld exponential is a meromorphic lattice sum whose value at zero is the Cauchy differential. Its Taylor coefficients give the higher-weight lattice differentials. For sign-normalized Hayes modules with free period lattice, an ordinary Hilbert-class trace after projection to powers divisible by $q^{\mathrm{N}}-1$ generates ideal values at $n\equiv1\pmod{q^{\mathrm{N}}-1}$. An algebraic parameter rescaling gives a trace formula for character-twisted values at $n\equiv1\pmod{q-1}$. The exact coefficient fields explain the difference between these weight ranges. For sign-normalized modules, decomposition by ideal classes also relates the element-type and ideal-type series at every positive weight. Explicit computations include the Hu--Huang--Yau module with nonprincipal period lattice and an elliptic curve with an infinite point of degree three, including the holomorphic term of its Cauchy differential. At rational infinity, the elliptic formula recovers the Green--Papanikolas identity.

papers.title: Prekosmic Grothendieck/Galois Categories
papers.abstract: We develop a theory on duality between groups and the categories of their representations, by providing an abstract characterization of such categories. The theory has two parallel formulations, each presenting a duality analogous to one of the two that were originally proposed by Grothendieck: the one between profinite groups and the abstract categories of their continuous representations on finite sets, and the other between affine group schemes over a field and the abstract categories of their finite-dimensional linear representations. In the present theory, groups and their representations are internal to a symmetric monoidal base category, with no finiteness condition imposed. The role of a fiber functor is played by a fiber point, an abstraction of the forgetful functor with its chosen adjoint. Over each base, a group determines the category of its representations equipped with the canonical fiber point, and a pointed abstract category determines the group that represents the presheaf of automorphisms of its chosen fiber point. These constructions yield mutually quasi-inverse equivalences of $(2,1)$-categories. By introducing change of base, we gather the dualities over individual bases into a single duality in each formulation. For a pointed abstract category, fiber points of the category are in perfect correspondence with torsors under the group associated to the chosen point. As an illustration of the theory, we reformulate the Galois theory of covering spaces for nonempty, path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected spaces.

papers.title: Principal bundles in supersymmetry
papers.abstract: We discuss rather basic problems on super principal bundles for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds (over $\mathbb{R}$) and analytic supermanifolds over a complete field of arbitrary characteristic. Sharper answers are obtained for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds and for homogeneous supermanifolds. Among others, it is proved for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds that given a $C^{\infty}$-supermanifold $B$ and a super Lie group $G$, there is a natural one-to-one correspondence (up to isomorphism) between the $G$-super principal bundles over $B$ and the $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$-principal bundles over $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$, where $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$ (resp., $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$) denotes the ordinary Lie group (resp., manifold) associated with $G$ (resp., $B$). To prove this, we show a generalized, equivariant version of the renowned Batchelor Theorem.

papers.title: Projective Decomposition and Intersection Cohomology of Rigid Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove a rigid analytic analogue of the Beilinson--Bernstein--Deligne decomposition theorem for projective morphisms over $p$-adic fields, with $\mathbf{Q}_\ell$-coefficients for every prime $\ell$, including $\ell=p$. As an application, we show that the $p$-adic intersection cohomology of every proper rigid analytic space is de Rham. We also establish an independent criterion for de Rham intersection cohomology with local coefficients in terms of the dimension of the boundary, yielding further results for curves, surfaces, and finite covers. For finite coefficients of characteristic different from $p$, we obtain isotropic analytic upper bounds for singular support and prove that singular support is analytic and Lagrangian for complexes supported in dimension at most one.

papers.title: PTOPOFL: Topology-Guided Personalised Federated Learning with Persistent-Homology Client Descriptors
papers.abstract: Clustered and personalised federated learning (FL) needs a signal telling the server which clients should share a model. Most methods derive it from losses or model updates that must be recomputed during training. We study pTopoFL, which derives it once, before training, from a compact persistent-homology (PH) descriptor of each client's feature distribution: the server clusters clients on these descriptors, weights them within clusters, and runs blended clustered local gradient descent, returning one personalised model per cluster. For strongly convex, smooth losses we analyse the complete procedure: for any partition, one round is a contraction with factor (1-eta*mu)^tau; the fixed point is characterised by a local-step drift bound, an exact formula for the effective strength of blending (which yields a calibration rule) and a stochastic floor exposing a bias-variance trade-off of clustering; and personalisation lowers the heterogeneity floor in proportion to a measurable share of the dispersion of client optima. Experiments on synthetic federations, a label-skew benchmark and a real four-hospital dataset confirm the theory and delimit the method. When feature geometry and decision rules co-vary, the PH partition recovers the latent client groups, including differences a linear-subspace descriptor misses, and pTopoFL is competitive with the strongest clustered baselines; on the real federation it lowers the test log-loss of FedAvg from 0.463 to 0.438, on par with the best personalised methods. When heterogeneity is invisible in feature geometry, it offers no advantage over FedAvg. pTopoFL transmits model parameters and is no more private than FedAvg; we give a record-level differential-privacy accounting and show that privatising the descriptor destroys the partition. Code reproduces every number.

papers.title: Quantum index, Arnold-Rokhlin surfaces, and real enumerative geometry
papers.abstract: The main goal of this note is to relate two different Welschinger-type rules of signs that were used for definition of real enumerative invariants of toric surfaces (the invariants considered being relative to the toric boundary). The relation between them intertwines Mikhalkin's quantum index and geometry of real and complex point sets of counted real curves. As a by-product, we suggest a new definition of quantum index, which can be used for refined invariant enumeration of real algebraic curves on surfaces in a non-toric setup.

papers.title: Quantum symmetric spaces at roots of 1
papers.abstract: We study the integral form of quantized coordinate algebras of symmetric spaces and its specializations at roots of unity. Our main tool is an integral localization, whose classical specialization recovers the open Borel orbit in the symmetric space. At a suitable odd root of unity, we prove that the quantum symmetric space is a finite projective module over its Frobenius center, which is canonically isomorphic to the classical coordinate algebra of the symmetric space. We show that the fibre algebras are isomorphic along each double Bruhat cell of the symmetric space. We determine the PI degree and propose a conjectural dimension formula for irreducible modules. In the simply connected case, we introduce a framed Kac-Moody data, which leads to a description of fibre algebras of quantum symmetric spaces via those of quantum Schubert cells.

papers.title: Quotient Geometry and Persistence-Stable Metrics for Swarm Configurations
papers.abstract: Can temporal information recover geometry lost by a persistence diagram? For $n\ge3$ points on the unit sphere evolving under known homogeneous complete consensus, we prove generic local recovery modulo rotations and permutations from two ordinary zero-dimensional Vietoris--Rips persistence snapshots. The structural result applies to every labeled tree: its edge inner products and their first temporal derivatives have differential rank $2n-3$, exactly the dimension of the regular formation quotient. An explicit pole--equator witness proves this simultaneously for all tree types after taking a finite intersection of open dense sets. Although one snapshot has generic local fibers of dimension $n-2$, two sufficiently close snapshots are injective on a common neighborhood. The optimal inverse Lipschitz constant grows as $\Theta(1/|h|)$ when the sampling interval tends to zero. A verified left inverse, interval derivative bounds, and explicit persistence-matching margins certify neighborhoods and time intervals at rational reference formations. The results are local and model-specific; reflection ambiguity and centered rank obstructions remain.

papers.title: Ramanujan Conjecture and Riemann Hypothesis for the unitary groups over function fields
papers.abstract: We establish generic local and global Langlands functoriality, namely stable base change, for the unitary groups in characteristic $p$. Main applications are the Ramanujan Conjecture and the Riemann Hypothesis for extended Langlands-Shahidi $L$-functions of the unitary groups over function fields.

papers.title: Rank and Border Rank Additivity of Complex Tensors with a Hankel Summand
papers.abstract: We prove that the CP rank of a complex Hankel tensor of order $m\ge3$ is additive with that of every complex tensor of the same order. Together with the known equality of CP and symmetric ranks for complex Hankel tensors, this yields symmetric rank additivity whenever the other summand has equal CP and symmetric ranks. We also prove that ordinary and symmetric border ranks coincide and are additive on direct sums of complex Hankel tensors of any common order at least three. Their common value is the sum of the middle binary catalecticant ranks. For order three, we further prove border-rank additivity when the other summand has border rank at most three, or is symmetric with at most five essential variables.

papers.title: Rational chain connectedness in the complex analytic setting
papers.abstract: We extend Hacon--M\textsuperscript{c}Kernan's rational chain connectedness theorem to the complex analytic setting. As a consequence, we prove that the fibers of any resolution of singularities of complex analytic kawamata log terminal singularities are rationally chain connected. In contrast to the original approach, we avoid the use of extension theorems and instead rely on the minimal model program.

papers.title: Rational Points on Drinfeld Modular Curves of Prime Level
papers.abstract: Let $q \ge 3$ be a prime power and let $\mathfrak{p} \subset \mathbf{F}_q[T]$ be a nonzero prime ideal of degree $d$. We prove that $Y_0(\mathfrak{p})(\mathbf{F}_q(T))=\emptyset$ if $d \ge 4$ is even or $d>q$, and that $Y_1(\mathfrak{p})(\mathbf{F}_q(T)) = \emptyset $ for every $d \ge 3$.

papers.title: Reconstruction of tensor categories of type $G_2$
papers.abstract: We prove that any ribbon tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ with the fusion rules of the compact group of type $G_2$ is equivalent to the representation category of the corresponding Drinfeld-Jimbo quantum group for $q^2=1$ or $q^2$ not a root of unity. We also prove an analogous result for the corresponding ribbon fusion tensor categories at roots of unity.

papers.title: Rigidity of algebraic sets with small distortion
papers.abstract: We prove that for positive integers $k$, $n$, and $d>1$, there is a maximal $c(k,n,d)>1$ such that if $X \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ is a connected $k$-dimensional complex algebraic set with degree at most $d$ and $dist(X) < c(k,n,d)$, then $X$ must be a complex affine linear subspace, where $dist(X)$ denotes the distortion of $X$ and is given by the supremum of the ratios $d_{inner}(p, q)/d_{outer}(p, q)$ for all $p,q\in X$ with $p\not= q$. We also prove that $c(1,n,d)=\sqrt{2}$ for any positive integers $k$ and $n$. This result provides a sharp rigidity phenomenon for curves in the $c$-LNE category, showing that near-isometric behavior of the inner and outer metrics forces the curve to be as simple as possible.

papers.title: Schur--Weyl duality for diagonalizing a Markov chain on the hypercube
papers.abstract: We show how the tools of modern algebraic combinatorics -- representation theory, Murphy elements, and particularly Schur--Weyl duality -- can be used to give an explicit orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions for a "curiously slowly mixing Markov chain" on the space of binary $n$-tuples. The basis is used to give sharp rates of convergence to stationarity.

papers.title: Searching Schemes With $p$-Adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems
papers.abstract: Firstly, for branched covering maps $f\colon Y\to X$ between smooth, separated schemes of finite type over the integral ring $O_K$ of a non-archimedean local field $K$, the ramification divisor is found to coincide with the divisor of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the Radon measure associated with an algebraic differential form on $Y$ against the pullback measure of one on $X$, both taking Borel sets of the space $Y(O_K)$ of $O_K$-rational points of $Y$ as input values. Secondly, the ultracontractivity of semigroups generated by Laplacian integral operators having a geodetic-distance-power kernel function is proven, using heat kernel estimates for ultrametric operators on $p$-adic balls. Thirdly, a series of $p$-adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems, depending on algebraic and pluricanonical differential forms with poles on spaces $X(O_K)$ coming from schemes is formulated and solved, extending previous work of the author. These results are then used to solve reconstruction problems on schemes: the divisor of a pluricanonical form with poles with at worst log-terminal singularities, as well as Weierstrass points of projective algebraic curves can be reconstructed via repeatedly finding weak solutions of $p$-adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems.

papers.title: Semi-supervised learning on singular data sets
papers.abstract: We propose to model singular data clouds by subanalytic sets, and develop an approach to semi-supervised learning in this setting. It relies on a Morrey-type embedding for Sobolev spaces relative to globally subanalytic measures with possibly singular support. As an illustration, we present a greedy method based on a Monte Carlo approximation of the Sobolev norm of the candidate solutions. We report numerical experiments on point clouds sampled from real algebraic varieties, as well as a test on a classification problem based on MNIST images downsampled into $7\times7$.

papers.title: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
papers.abstract: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation \`{a} la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.

papers.title: Simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalences for tensor categories
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate monoidal derived equivalences between tensor categories with infinitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects. We introduce the notion of a simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalence and prove that a simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalence gives rise to a tensor equivalence. In addition, we investigate which tensor categories have the property that every monoidal derived equivalence between them is necessarily simple-shifted, and we establish some sufficient conditions for this property. As a corollary, we show that a monoidal derived equivalence between pointed tensor categories implies a tensor equivalence between them.

papers.title: Singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type and standard eventually homological isomorphisms
papers.abstract: We refine the definition of eventually homological isomorphisms so that it becomes more natural and fruitful. We introduce singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type which can be viewed as standard singular equivalences of different levels and are more convenient for reducing various homological conjectures and transferring homological properties. We develop the theories of singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type for $n\ge 2$ and standard eventually homological isomorphisms between derived categories by giving their characterizations in terms of $\otimes$-(co)perfect complexes of bimodules, two constructions via opposite algebras and tensor product algebras, examples induced by homomorphisms of algebras and idempotents, and applications to the reduction of homological conjectures such as the finitistic dimension conjecture, Gorenstein symmetry conjecture and Auslander-Reiten conjecture, as well as to the preservation of homological properties such as Gorensteinness, the Fg condition, Happel's property and Han's property. Moreover, we show that essentially surjective standard eventually homological isomorphisms between derived categories correspond to standard singular equivalences with canonical left adjoint.

papers.title: Socle formulas for rigid irreducible components of Lusztig's nilpotent varieties in type $A$
papers.abstract:
Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field. For any irreducible component $C$ of a nilpotent variety of type $A$ let $\pi(C)$ be the irreducible representation of a general linear group over $F$ attached to it. We show that if the multisegment of $C$ is multiplicity free, $C$ is rigid if and only if $\pi(C)$ is $\square$-irreducible. In this case, \[
  \pi(C*D)=soc\bigl(\pi(C)\times\pi(D)\bigr),\qquad
  \pi(D*C)=soc\bigl(\pi(D)\times\pi(C)\bigr) \] for every irreducible component $D$, where $*$ is the binary operation defined by Aizenbud and Lapid, in accordance with a conjecture of Lapid and M\'inguez.
  We also give a computer-assisted example in $A_7$ of a non-simple rigid module $z\ne0$ which does not admit a proper rigid submodule $y\ne0$ such that $Ext_\Pi^1(z,z/y)=0$, answering negatively a question of Aizenbud and Lapid.

papers.title: Some Cubic and Quartic Inequalities of Four Variables
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H} \subset \mathcal{H}_{n,d} := \mathbb{R}[x_1$,$\ldots$, $x_n]_d$ be a vector space, and $A$ be a compact semialgebraic subset of $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{R}}^{n-1}$. We shall study some PSD cones $\mathcal{P} = \mathcal{P}(A$, $\mathcal{H}) := \big\{f \in \mathcal{H}$ $\big|$ $f(a) \geq 0$ ($\forall a \in A$)$\big\}$. Our interests are (1) to determine the extremal elements of $\mathcal{P}$, (2) to determine discriminants of $\mathcal{P}$, (3) to describe $\mathcal{P}$ as a union of basic semialgebraic subsets, and (4) to find a nice test set when $\dim \mathcal{H}$ is low. In this article, we present (1), (2), (3) and (4) for $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^4$, $\mathcal{H}_{4,4}^{s0})$ and $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}_+^4$, $\mathcal{H}_{4,4}^{s0})$, where $\mathcal{H}_{n,d}^{s0} := \big\{f \in \mathcal{H}_{n,d}$ $\big|$ $f$ is symmetric and $f(1,\ldots,1)=0 \big\}$. We also provide (1) -- (4) for $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}_+^4$, $\mathcal{H}_{4,3}^{c0})$, where $\mathcal{H}_{n,d}^{c0} := \big\{f \in \mathcal{H}_{n,d}$ $\big|$ $f$ is cyclic and $f(1,\ldots,1)=0 \big\}$.

papers.title: Spectral Curves for Semisimple Conformal Frobenius Manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct connected spectral curves for semisimple conformal Frobenius manifolds with flat unit, using the periods of the second structure equation. Eynard-Orantin topological recursion on these curves reproduces the stable ancestor correlators of Givental-Teleman reconstruction. The spectral curves are defined on simply connected domains in the complex plane. We apply the construction to the quantum cohomology of $\mathbb P^n$ for $n\ge2$ at a point, obtaining explicit spectral curve data in terms of Hecke triangle groups and hypergeometric functions. Finally, for $\mathbb P^2$ and $\mathbb P^3$, we express the complete spectral curve data, including the bidifferentials, in classical modular and quasimodular forms.

papers.title: Split Normal Bundles and Rigidity of Holomorphic Immersions from Compact Ball Quotients
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic immersion from a compact complex hyperbolic space form into a higher-dimensional complex hyperbolic space form. We prove that if the normal bundle decomposes as a direct sum of holomorphic line bundles, then the immersion is totally geodesic. This result has no restriction on the codimension and extends, under the splitting hypothesis, the classical rigidity theorem of Cao--Mok. The proof uses the polarized complex variation of Hodge structure induced from the target. The line-bundle decomposition produces nef zero-Higgs line quotients, and a Chern-character identity forces the Gauss-defect form to have nontrivial nullity at every point. The null-foliation and boundary argument of Cao--Mok then shows that the defect vanishes identically. In particular, this answers a question posed by Mok almost twenty years ago about decomposable normal bundles for complex surfaces immersed in four-dimensional complex hyperbolic space forms.

papers.title: Splitting vector bundles over real algebraic varieties
papers.abstract:
Suppose $X$ is a smooth affine real variety and $\mathscr{E}$ is a vector bundle over $X$. We analyze the problem of splitting off a free rank one summand from $\mathscr{E}$ in corank $0$ and $1$. The problem in corank $0$ can be viewed as the search for a real analog of Murthy's celebrating splitting theorem in the algebraically closed case: to wit, beyond the vanishing of the top Chern class in Chow theory, are the obstructions to splitting ``purely topological''? In a sense, the answer in this case is yes, and we give a proof, using motivic techniques, of a mild extension of the results of Bhatwadekar-Sridharan and Bhatwadekar-Das-Mandal.
  In corank $1$, in the algebraically closed situation, Murthy's splitting conjecture (now a theorem in characteristic $0$) predicts that the vanishing of the top Chern class in Chow theory is the only obstruction to splitting off a free rank $1$ summand, and we can search for a suitable ``real'' analog of this assertion. We observe that several natural guesses for a ``real'' analog of Murthy's splitting conjecture cannot be true, i.e., that the situation over the real numbers is rather complicated.

papers.title: Stevens' Approach to Kloosterman Sums on Split Groups
papers.abstract: We develop a uniform framework for Stevens' approach to Kloosterman sums on split groups over $p$-adic fields. The main result reduces the bounding of Kloosterman sums to that for the so-called Pl\"ucker-constrained sets, which are certain subsets of affine spaces constrained by conditions giving by the Pl\"ucker coordinates. We then give a nontrivial bound for the Kloosterman sums on the exceptional group $G_2$. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions associated with generic representations on $G_2$.

papers.title: Strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Actions and Symmetric Chain Decompositions
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of a strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action on a poset, and conjecture the existence of such an action is equivalent to the existence of a symmetric chain decomposition of that poset. We explain the intuition behind the conjecture, go through a number of explicit examples, and prove some special cases and relaxations of the conjecture. Then we explain a computational experiment where we tested the conjecture on millions of randomly constructed rank-symmetric, rank-unimodal, and strongly Sperner posets.

papers.title: Sumsets regularity versus Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for monomial curves
papers.abstract: Let $A=\{0=a_0<a_1<\dots<a_{k-1}=d\}$ be integers with greatest common divisor $1$, let $C_A$ be the projective monomial curve they define, and let $\mathrm{reg}(A)$ be the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of its coordinate ring. Gimenez and Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez proved $\mathrm{reg}(A)\le\sigma(A)+1$ for the sumsets regularity $\sigma(A)$; the reverse inequality $\sigma(A)\le\mathrm{reg}(A)$ was proposed as an open conjecture in a 2024 talk. We show that it fails and measure by how much. Let $c_1,c_2$ be the conductors of the two numerical semigroups attached to $A$ and $N=\lceil(c_1+c_2)/d\rceil$. For curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ that are not arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, $\mathrm{reg}(A)\ge(c_1+c_2)/d+2$, with equality exactly for the arithmetically Buchsbaum curves, and $\sigma(A)=\mathrm{reg}(A)$. For arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ we prove $9N\le10\,\mathrm{reg}(A)-2$, with $9/10$ best possible, and give an explicit family with $\sigma(A)-\mathrm{reg}(A)$ unbounded. In $\mathbb{P}^4$ a family with a band-shaped Ap\'ery set has $\mathrm{reg}(A)/\sigma(A)\to(2+\sqrt2)/4$ along the solutions of a Pell equation, and gluing carries this bound to every $\mathbb{P}^r$ with $r\ge5$.

papers.title: Super Howe duality and rigidity of hybrid Fourier transforms
papers.abstract: We characterize the hybrid Fourier transform on the Schwartz--Grassmann space $\caS(\bbR^m)\otimes\Lambda_{2n}$ by operator intertwining relations. Using the bosonic oscillator Howe decomposition and the fermionic Lefschetz decomposition, we describe the action of the hybrid Fourier transform on both tensor factors. We show that first-order covariance with respect to coordinate multiplication and differentiation determines the transform up to a scalar. For $m,n\ge1$, we prove that covariance under all even quadratic operators, together with any one nonzero mixed quadratic operator, determines the linear span of the hybrid Fourier transform and its inverse. This rigidity result is obtained by computing the ordinary commutants of the even and full quadratic oscillator actions of $\fosp(4n|2m)$. After a degree-scaling change of normalization, we make the hybrid Fourier transform unitary with respect to the occupation number inner product, and factor it into a bosonic oscillator rotation and (up to a scalar phase) an $SU(2)$ rotation in the fermionic Lefschetz representation. For $m=1$ and $n\ge2$, we show that full even quadratic covariance together with the parity-preserving cubic relation for $qQ_f$ determines the unitary transform up to a global phase and a fermion-parity phase. Finally we calculate the unitary conjugation formulas for Hubbard--Holstein Hamiltonian for a hybrid continuous-variable and discrete-variable quantum system.

papers.title: Superschemes and supermanifolds with free $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-action
papers.abstract: We prove that given an analytic supermanifold $X$ over a complete field on which the additive supergroup $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ of super-dimension $0|n$ acts freely (in an appropriate sense), the quotient $X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ exists as an analytic supermanifold, and the canonical morphism $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ is an $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-principal bundle. A stronger version of this result is proven for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds, whereby $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$ is a trivial $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-principal bundle. Previously, Polishchuk [18] established an algebro-geometric analogue, which proves that a superscheme $X$ with free $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-action gives rise to a locally trivial $\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$-torsor $X \to X/\mathbb{A}^{0|n}$. This result is proven here in an alternative, elementary way. To all of these, a Hopf-algebraic approach is effectively employed.

papers.title: Terao's freeness conjecture for arrangements of 15 and 16 lines
papers.abstract: We prove that Terao's freeness conjecture holds for arrangements of 15 and of 16 lines in the complex projective plane. Together with the theorem of Barakat and K\"uhne for at most 14 hyperplanes, this shows that freeness of a central arrangement of at most 16 planes in $\mathbb{C}^3$ is determined by its intersection lattice. The proof has a theoretical and a computational part. Combining published combinatorial criteria for freeness (due to Abe, Dimca, Dimca-K\"uhne-Pokora and Yoshinaga) with Bojanowski's Hirzebruch-type inequality and an elementary counting identity, we show that a counterexample would have exponents $(6,8)$ or $(7,7)$ for 15 lines and $(7,8)$ for 16 lines, and an intersection lattice subject to strong numerical constraints. We then enumerate all 22,544,280 simple rank 3 matroids satisfying these constraints, up to isomorphism, and determine the complex realization space of each of them exactly over $\mathbb{Q}$. Exactly eleven of them are realizable over $\mathbb{C}$, and on each of these the freeness of the realizations is constant. As a by-product we classify the free arrangements of 15 and 16 lines that are not divisionally free, have maximal multiplicity smaller than the smaller nontrivial exponent, and have at least four intersection points on every line.

papers.title: Terminal Coalgebras in Countably Many Steps
papers.abstract:
We present a collection of results that imply that an endofunctor on a category has a terminal coalgebra obtainable as a countable limit of its terminal-coalgebra chain. This holds for finitary endofunctors on locally finitely presentable categories under conditions on both the functor and the category. We adapt finiteness arguments that were originally advanced by Worrell concerning terminal coalgebras for finitary set functors. Examples include the categories of sets, posets, vector spaces, graphs, nominal sets, and presheaves on finite sets. Worrell also described, without proof, the terminal-coalgebra chain of the finite power-set functor. We provide a detailed proof following his ideas.
  We then turn to polynomial endofunctors on the categories of Hausdorff topological spaces and metric spaces. The Vietoris space of compact subsets yields an endofunctor $\mathscr{V}$ on the category of Hausdorff spaces. Vietoris polynomial endofunctors are built from $ \mathscr{V}$, the identity and constant functors by forming products, coproducts and compositions. Their terminal coalgebras are obtained in $\omega$ steps. We then turn to the class of Hausdorff polynomial functors on the category of metric spaces, which is analogous but uses in lieu of $\mathscr{V}$ the Hausdorff functor $\mathcal{H}$. We prove they have terminal coalgebras obtained in $\omega + \omega$ steps. Finally, we show that every finitary endofunctor on the category of vector spaces over a fixed field again has a terminal coalgebra obtained in $\omega+\omega$ steps.

papers.title: The 3-adic Steinberg block and a categorical 3-adic local Langlands correspondence for $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_3)$
papers.abstract: We extend the work of Johansson-Newton-Wang-Erickson on a categorical $p$-adic Langlands correspondence over $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ to $p = 3$ by recontextualizing their construction in the Steinberg case. We produce a novel, more categorical method of analyzing the properties of this construction without requiring an explicit algebraic presentation. As input to this argument, we also perform some new analysis of the representation theory of the $3$-adic Steinberg block of $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_3)$, obtaining results complementing those of Pa\v{s}k\={u}nas.

papers.title: The associated graded algebras of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras
papers.abstract: For any finite-dimensional algebra $A$, one can associate a graded algebra (denoted by $\mathrm{gr}(A)$) with the radical filtration of $A$. An interesting question is to compare the representation theories of $A$ and $\mathrm{gr}(A)$. When $A$ is a Brauer graph algebra with defining Brauer graph $\Gamma$, we have described the representation type of $\mathrm{gr}(A)$ in terms of the information of $\Gamma$. In this paper, we describe the representation type of $\mathrm{gr}(A)$ when $A$ is a biserial fractional Brauer graph algebra - a notion that properly generalizes a Brauer graph algebra - in terms of the information of the defining biserial fractional Brauer graph $\Gamma$ of $A$.

papers.title: The big cactus group, invariant tensors, and rectangular tableaux
papers.abstract: The cactus group acts on tensor products of crystals and, through Bender--Knuth involutions, on semistandard Young tableaux. We show that the big cactus group $J'_n=\pi_1^{\mathfrak S_n}(\overline M_{0,n}(\mathbb R))$, $n\ge3$, is obtained from the cactus group by imposing $n-1$ Dynkin-reversal relations, which say that conjugation by the full reversal acts on the Bender--Knuth generators by the Dynkin diagram automorphism; the quotient map is induced by forgetting the distinguished marked point. We give a second presentation, in which these relations are replaced by the requirement that every reduced word for the longest element of $\mathfrak S_n$ adapted to an orientation of $A_{n-1}$ represents the full reversal. These relations also hold on rectangular tableaux, where every adapted reduced word therefore acts as evacuation, and on invariant tensors: for finite normal crystals of any complex semisimple Lie algebra, the cactus action on invariants factors through $J'_n$. We prove the latter combinatorially in type $A$ and in general via Gaudin eigenline coverings. Haiman's promotion relation follows from a single adapted-word relation, but for $n\ge4$ it is strictly weaker than the whole family.

papers.title: The blow-up of the cubic fourfold along eight planes is Fano
papers.abstract: We prove that the blow-up Z_m of a smooth cubic fourfold along m <= 8 planes, pairwise meeting at distinct points and satisfying explicit generality conditions, is a smooth Fano fourfold of Picard rank rho(Z_m) = m+1 <= 9; in particular, we obtain three new families of smooth Fano fourfolds with rho > 6 that are not a product of surfaces. Complementary to this result, we show that a smooth cubic fourfold as above exists. Moreover, we study the birational geometry of Z_m and show that it corresponds exactly to that of a smooth del Pezzo surfaces S_m, obtained as the blow-up of P^2 along m <= 8 points in general position. Namely, Z_m and S_m have isomorphic Mori cones, pseudo-effective cones with same Mori chamber decomposition, and there is a one-to-one correspondence between the contractions of Z_m and the contractions of S_m. Lastly, we study the anticanonical linear system of Z_m and prove that it is basepoint free if and only if m <= 7. For m = 8 and a special configuration of planes, we show that the anticanonical base locus Bs(|-K_{Z_8}|) has dimension 2 and contains a smooth del Pezzo surface of degree 1.

papers.title: The Casimir on the $K$-fixed tensor square of the minimal representation of $G_{2(2)}$
papers.abstract: We compute the quadratic Casimir on the $K$-fixed subspace of the Hilbert tensor square of the unitary minimal representation of the split real group $G_{2(2)}$. In an explicit algebraic basis of invariant tensors, the Casimir acts by a three-term recurrence. Normalizing this basis yields a symmetric Jacobi operator whose self-adjoint realization is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by $-\frac92-8x^2$ in a Wilson-polynomial model with parameters $(\frac34,\frac34,\frac7{12},\frac{11}{12})$. We give the normalized spectral density and the unitary transform. The resulting spectrum is purely absolutely continuous, equals $(-\infty,-\frac92]$, and has scalar spectral multiplicity one.

papers.title: The center conjecture for cyclotomic Hecke algebras and cohomology of quiver varieties
papers.abstract:
