For a quiver without edge loops, we construct an isomorphism from the cohomology of a Nakajima quiver variety with coefficients in an arbitrary field to the Jucys--Murphy center of the corresponding cyclotomic KLR algebra over that field. In affine type $A^{(1)}_{e-1}$, combining this with a dimension count shows that this Jucys--Murphy center coincides with the full center in characteristic $0$, when the characteristic does not divide $e$, and when the characteristic equals $e$. This follows from a geometric theorem showing that the sum of these cohomology rings is cocyclic as a module over an integral form of a loop algebra.
  As a consequence, we prove that the center of a cyclotomic Hecke algebra of type $G(r,1,n)$ with $q\neq 1$ over any field is generated by symmetric polynomials in its Jucys--Murphy elements, and the same holds over any commutative domain in which $q-1$ is invertible. We also prove a generalization to the integral case of the conjecture of Krylov, Paegelow and Shlykov identifying the equivariant $K$-theory of the core of a Gieseker variety with the cocenter of the generic cyclotomic Hecke algebra, including the natural extension of this conjecture to positive characteristic.

papers.title: The Chern character of a coherent sheaf on a smooth projective hypersurface
papers.abstract: Given a coherent sheaf on a smooth projective hypersurface X, we prove an explicit formula for its Chern character as a Cech cocycle in terms of the free resolution of the associated module and calculate its image in the Jacobian ring under the Griffiths residue map. The formula is a geometric analogue of the Kapustin-Li formula for Landau-Ginzburg models, but proven directly using Hodge-theoretic techniques. This yields an effective method to compute the primitive part of the Chern character of any coherent sheaf using commutative algebra. We finish by proving the Hodge conjecture for the degree 33 Fermat fourfold.

papers.title: The classification of taut surface singularities via representations from logarithmic vector fields
papers.abstract: We study logarithmic vector fields on exceptional cycles through finite-dimensional representations and recover Laufer's classification of taut normal complex surface singularities. For graphs with two nodes, restriction maps define representations of a fixed quiver, with dimensions bounded independently of the number of components and their self-intersections. We identify restriction cohomology with an extension group and use interval decomposition to reduce its vanishing to interpolation on a rational chain. These calculations determine the classification conditions, and vanishing on every analytic realization proves sufficiency, including the nonrational cases. The obstruction cycles also give a uniform criterion: a graph is taut if and only if $H^1(5E,S_X|_{5E})=0$ for every analytic realization, where $S_X$ is the ambient logarithmic tangent bundle. We prove that five is the smallest positive integer for which this criterion holds for all graphs.

papers.title: The first Cech derived functor
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a semi-abelian category, $\mathcal{D}$ a Birkhoff subcategory of $\mathcal{C}$, and $I$ the associated reflector. For $C\in \mathcal{C}$, we establish an isomorphism between $\mathrm{H}_1(\mathrm{N}(I(\check{C}(f,C))))$ (where $\mathrm{N}$ is the Moore normalization functor and $\check{C}(f,C)$ is a Cech resolution associated to $C$) and $\mathrm{H}_1(\mathrm{N}(I(\mathbb{G}(C))))$ (where $\mathbb{G}(C)$ is the canonical $\mathbb{G}$-simplicial resolution of $C$ for $\mathbb{G}$ the comonad derived from an adjunction $F\colon \mathcal{X}\to \mathcal{C}\dashv U\colon \mathcal{C}\to \mathcal{X}$ satisfying classical conditions introduced by Quillen). The former corresponds to the Hopf formula for the second homology object associated to $I$, while the latter represents the first \v Cech derived functor of $I$. Specifically, we show that both can be expressed by a single unified formula.
  Furthermore, we can also prove that, under certain assumptions, the first \v Cech derived functor of $I$ is naturally isomorphic to the first non-additive derived functor of $I$ (in the sense of Culot--Renaud--Van~der~Linden).

papers.title: The genus of a curve on Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Calabi-Yau variety of dimension $3$, with Picard number one. Let $n$ be the self-intersection of the ample generator of the N\'eron-Severi group of $X$. Let $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}$ be the Gopakumar-Vafa invariant of $X$ of genus $g$ and degree $d$. It is conjectured that {\it if $g>\frac{d^{2}}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$, then $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}=0$}. In this paper, we prove the implication when $d\gg n$ and $X\subset \mathbb P^r$ is a complete intersection in projective space. The vanishing follows by proving that if $C$ is a closed subscheme of $X$ of dimension $1$, arithmetic genus $p_a(C)$, and degree $d\gg n$, then $p_a(C) \leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$. Actually, we prove a somewhat more general result. In particular, we prove that $C$ is an extremal curve if and only if $C$ is the complete intersection on $X$ with a hyperplane $H$ and a hypersurface $F$, namely $C=X\cap H\cap F$.

papers.title: The Riemann theta function near soliton limit
papers.abstract: It has been known that (the square of) Jacobi elliptic function can be expressed by an infinite sum of single solitons of $\sech^2$ shape. In this paper, we show that there exists a similar structure for higher genus cases. It turns out that this is just a consequence of the quasi-periodicity of the Riemann $\theta$-function. More precisely, we show that the second derivative of $\log \theta$ with the \emph{real} Riemann $\theta$-function of genus $g$ near soliton limit can be well approximated by the \emph{sum} of \emph{real} and \emph{regular} $g$-soliton solutions of Hirota-type in $g$-dimensional real space $\R^g$. This leads to a tessellation of $\R^g$, whose tile is an oblique prism divided into $2^g$ sections by hyper-planes of dominant exponents in the theta function. We apply the results to study quasi-periodic solutions to the KdV and KP equations. We construct the quasi-periodic solutions using the Schottky group, which uniformizes the corresponding Riemann surfaces. We also discuss solitons on quasi-periodic background by pinching some of the homological cycles

papers.title: The section conjecture for generic pointed curves
papers.abstract: Let $k/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated, let $g\geq3$ and $n\geq1$, and let $\mathcal M_{g,n/k}$ be the moduli stack of smooth proper genus-$g$ curves with $n$ distinct ordered markings. Put $K=k(\mathcal M_{g,n/k})$. We prove Grothendieck's section conjecture for the generic $n$-pointed genus-$g$ curve over $K$. Over both the moduli stack and its function field, the continuous sections of the arithmetic fundamental-group extension of the universal complete curve are, up to geometric conjugacy, exactly the $n$ tautological sections. The same classification holds for every geometrically pro-$\ell$ quotient, for every prime $\ell$. Together with Hain's determination of the rational points, these classifications give examples over fields finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$ with any prescribed positive number of rational points for which the full section conjecture holds. The proof builds on Hain's weighted-completion and nonabelian cohomology methods, with a hyperelliptic calculation providing the genus-three input. An integral normalizer lemma and moving-mark arguments pass from unipotent sections to geometrically pro-$\ell$ sections. Configuration spaces and Mochizuki's open Hom theorem yield the full profinite classification, and generic descent identifies the section classes over the moduli stack with those over $K$.

papers.title: The truncated symbol of a differential symmetry breaking operator
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we introduce the truncated symbol of a differential symmetry breaking operator between parabolically induced representations. This generalizes the symbol map, which is defined for the case of abelian nilpotent radicals, to the non-abelian setting. The inverse of the truncated symbol map enables one to develop a recipe for the F-method for any nilpotent radical.
  As an application, we classify and construct differential intertwining operators on the full flag variety $SL(3,\mathbb{R})/B$ and homomorphisms between Verma modules. It turned out that, surprisingly, Cayley continuants appeared in the coefficients of one of the five families of operators that we constructed. At the end of the paper, factorization identities for the differential operators and homomorphisms are also classified. Binary Krawtchouk polynomials play a key role in the proof.

papers.title: The two-step spectral locus of the octonionic structure operator
papers.abstract: We continue the study of the octonionic spectrum of the octonionic structure operator $h$ on $W=\mathbb O\otimes_{\mathbb R}V$, where $V$ is the seven-dimensional representation of $G_2$. The real spectrum and the octonionic one-step spectrum, given by the equation $h(w)=w\lambda$ for real or octonion $\lambda$, have been determined in earlier work. In this paper, we study the two-step equation $h(w)=(w\lambda_1)\lambda_2$. Due to non-associativity, this does not in general reduce to the one-step problem. An adapted quaternionic frame represents successive right multiplication by an operator with four real coefficients. The $SU(2)$ subgroup fixing the frame splits $W$ into invariant sectors of dimensions $16$, $12$ and $28$. We factor the determinant of the resulting 4-parameter operator pencil and characterize the pairs for which a nonzero solution exists. The singular locus of this pencil in $\mathbb R^4$ is the union of an explicit algebraic set and a round $3$-sphere. The $12$-dimensional sector carries the one-step problem at the reversed product $\lambda_2\lambda_1$. The $28$-dimensional sector contributes no additional real singular points; the fixed sector produces solutions even when neither product lies in the one-step right spectrum.

papers.title: The Yau Geometric Conjecture for Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: This paper presents a proof of the long-standing Yau Geometric Conjecture.

papers.title: Torelli theorem for the moduli spaces of twisted vector bundles on smooth projective curves
papers.abstract: We prove Torelli theorems for moduli space of twisted vector bundles on smooth projective curves over an arbitrary field of characteristic $\neq 2$. A twisted Hitchin construction recovers the curve in higher rank and degree, with partial recovery of the twisting class. For rank two with trivial determinant, we recover the curve and the Brauer class from the moduli stack through an ordered Kummer cover and its polarized Jacobian torsor. For odd determinant on hyperelliptic curves, residual gerbes give a relative Desale--Ramanan construction without an actual determinant line bundle over the ground field. An intrinsic polarized Fano torsor recovers the curve and the class, and a corrected polarization obstruction recovers the determinant gerbe. We also give a twisted Newstead construction in genus two, with an explicit descent condition for its converse, and period--index applications. This is the second part in a series of two papers.

papers.title: Torsion Cycles in Projective Threefolds:From Serre's Construction to Artin-Mumford
papers.abstract: The torsion subgroup of third integral cohomology is a birational invariant of smooth projective complex threefolds; its nonvanishing obstructs stable rationality. We recall a proof using Hironaka's elimination of indeterminacies and the integral blowup formula. The Godeaux--Serre construction and Poincar\'e duality imply that every finite abelian group is the third integral cohomology group of a smooth projective complex threefold. This classical realization also has a description through families of concurrent plane lines. Their incidence threefolds have smooth normalizations, obtained by an explicit blowup and described as projective-line bundles over smooth surfaces. The Lefschetz theorem determines the fundamental group of these surfaces, and the projective bundle formula computes the third cohomology. The resulting threefolds are birational to products of surfaces with the projective line, and their torsion three-cycles are represented by sphere bundles over loops. Examples and the comparison with the unirational Artin--Mumford threefold explain the role of the base surface and the distinction between smooth blowups and resolution of a singular space.

papers.title: Twisted Deligne modules and abelian varieties over finite fields
papers.abstract: Isogeny classes of abelian varieties over finite fields were described by Tate and Honda. Deligne proved that the category of ordinary abelian varieties over a finite field is equivalent to the category of ordinary Deligne modules. Centeleghe and Stix extended Deligne's results to the whole category of abelian varieties, but, if the base finite field is not prime, then the target category is not related to Deligne modules. In this paper we introduce generalized and twisted Deligne modules and give a more direct generalization of the Deligne theorem.

papers.title: Uniform vector bundles over $\mathbb{P}^4$
papers.abstract: There is a long-standing conjecture which states that every uniform algebraic vector bundle of rank $r<2n$ on the $n$-dimensional projective space $\mathbb{P}^n$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$ is homogeneous. This conjecture is valid for $n\leq3$. In this paper, we classify all uniform vector bundles of rank $r<8$ over $\mathbb{P}^4$ and show that the conjecture holds for $n=4$.

papers.title: Units of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant $K$-theory and bundles of UHF-algebras
papers.abstract: We consider infinite tensor product actions of a finite cyclic group $G$ on the UHF-algebra $D = \text{End}(V)^{\otimes \infty}$ for a finite-dimensional projectively faithful unitary $G$-representation $V$ and determine the equivariant homotopy type of the group $\text{Aut}(D \otimes \mathbb{K})$, where $\mathbb{K}$ are the compact operators on $\ell^2(G) \otimes H_0$ for a separable Hilbert space $H_0$ with $\dim(H_0) = \infty$. We show that this group carries an equivariant infinite loop space structure revealing it as the first space of a naive $G$-spectrum. We identify this spectrum with the positive units $gl_1(KU^D)_+$ of equivariant $KU^D$-theory, which was not possible in the case of circle actions considered by Evans and the second author. Here, $KU^D$ is a $G$-spectrum representing $X \mapsto K_*^G(C(X) \otimes D)$. As a consequence the first group of the cohomology theory associated to $gl_1(KU^D)_+$ classifies equivariant $D \otimes \mathbb{K}$-bundles over finite $G$-CW-complexes.

papers.title: Upper bounds on the number of images produced by point-mass lenses at different distances
papers.abstract: If a light source is sequentially lensed by $n$ intervening point-mass lenses at distinct distances, the number of isolated images for a generic source position cannot be greater than $2\cdot 3^{n-1}$. If lensing shear is present in each lens plane, the image counts could be as large as $4^n$, however. For a general multi-plane point-mass lens system, we also devise the recurrence for the BKK bound on the image counts, which is strictly less than Perry's bound due to the resultant degree for $n\ge 2$. None the less, this bound is still quadratic in the number of lenses on each plane, so is likely to overestimate the true sharp bound, which is expected to grow linearly with the number of lenses.

papers.title: Weighted homogeneous surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings
papers.abstract: We study rational homology disk smoothings through canonical-cover representations and specialization of reflexive canonical powers, and recover the known dual graph and analytic classification. The geometric-genus representation of the canonical covering group, together with its complex conjugate, is a direct summand of the reduced regular representation. Specialization forces the canonical Riemann--Roch corrections to vanish; explicit formulas give equations for the Seifert invariants. For three arms and central weight two, these equations, the character restrictions, and the numerical identities determine the Seifert data without assuming the existence of a smoothing. Projective compactifications treat the remaining cases, and elliptic pencils explain the four-arm attachment points and the parameter independence of their cross ratios. We construct strong $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein smoothings for all listed analytic structures by deforming canonical-cover equations and lifting generators of the full first syzygy module. The numerical Milnor formula gives rational homology disk fibers.

papers.title: Weights of KZ motives and quantum groups
papers.abstract:
The Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (KZ) connection is defined on the constant bundle determined by $n$ finite-dimensional irreducible representations of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and a nonzero complex parameter $\kappa$, over the configuration space of $n$ distinct points on the affine line. Work of Schechtman--Varchenko and Looijenga shows that, when $\kappa$ is rational, the resulting local systems admit natural motivic realizations, called KZ motives.
  The Kazhdan--Lusztig equivalence identifies the local systems underlying these motivic variations with certain representations of the pure braid group arising from the corresponding Lusztig quantum group at a root of unity. We formulate conjectures relating the weight filtrations of KZ motives to structures in quantum-group representation theory, particularly tilting modules and the Jantzen and Andersen filtrations, and provide evidence for these conjectures.
  Our methods use a new deformation of the representation ring that records the first moments of the weight filtration, together with Schmid's theorem on limiting mixed Hodge structures and results on the Hodge filtration obtained in earlier joint work with S. Mukhopadhyay.

papers.title: Zero-free half-planes for Hecke L-functions over number fields
papers.abstract: In [Liu26a], varying the length and moment parameters in the cubic-theta argument of [Ope26a] gave the zero-free half-plane $Re(s)>B_{\mathrm{new}}=0.874957019420098946\ldots$ for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and for Dirichlet $L$-functions, and its optimality in the specified exponent comparison system. In this paper, we extend the argument to finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over cyclotomic fields containing $\mu_{12}$ and, by class-field descent, to every pair $(K,\eta)$ whose cyclic class field has metabelian normal closure over $\mathbb Q$, including every finite-order character over every abelian number field. Then, adapting the averaged numerator estimate developed by Xu and Sang [XS26] for Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and combining it with a limiting contradiction argument, we obtain the boundary $B_\flat=0.874886647039964\ldots$, the root near $0.8749$ of $133488B^4-376596B^3+384534B^2-167541B+26231$; it is the exact infimum of the refined comparison system, unattained by finite chains starting above it. Since the analytic argument uses only $\mu_{12}\subset F$, we run it over $F=K(\zeta_{12})$ for an arbitrary number field $K$ and descend: every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over every number field is zero-free for $Re(s)>B_\flat$. The analytic argument uses the exceptional-theta constructions and local calculations of the preprint [Ope26b].
